title: 2002 HMMT February Algebra Problem 5
statement: Find the greatest common divisor of the numbers \(2002+2,2002^{2}+2,2002^{3}+2, \ldots\).

solutions.text: 6. Notice that \(2002+2\) divides \(2002^{2}-2^{2}\), so any common divisor of \(2002+2\) and \(2002^{2}+2\) must divide \(\left(2002^{2}+2\right)-\left(2002^{2}-2^{2}\right)=6\). On the other hand, every number in the sequence is even, and the \(n\)th number is always congruent to \(1^{n}+2 \equiv 0\) modulo 3 . Thus, 6 divides every number in the sequence.
